newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metals slip, no impact from Deng.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metals slip, no impact from Deng.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metal futures ended lower across the board on Thursday, the steepest falls being among platinum group metals, as weaker bullion prices and the yen's rise pressured the market, traders said.
The precious metals market shrugged off news of the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping.

Platinum and palladium futures extended early losses, depressed by heavy long-liquidation, as selling was partly stimulated by overnight news that the U.S. government would offer some of its stocks of platinum and palladium for sale on March 24.
Gold futures ranged from two to six yen per gram weaker, with benchmark December ending down two at 1,364 yen.
Spot gold was quoted at $344.70/345.00 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $345.00/345.50 in New York on Wednesday.

In a sluggish gold futures market, private investors were slightly on the selling side. "Private investors are not showing any interest in making fresh buying above the 1,360 yen level," one trader said. They were tending to hold a slightly bearish sentiment towards TOCOM gold, taking the view that the yen's further fall would be limited, they said.
